traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Confusing Sangam-era Cholas (Karikala) with Medieval-era Imperial Cholas (Rajaraja I).
Assuming Chola administration was purely centralized; it was actually decentralized and autonomous at the village level.
Mistaking temple inscriptions for mere religious texts; they are primary sources for economic and political land grants.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Core: Kaveri Delta (Tanjore/Thanjavur).
  • Coastal advantage: Coromandel Coast.
  • Naval reach: Bay of Bengal as 'Chola Lake'.

Personalities

  • Karikala: Built Kallanai dam.
  • Rajaraja I: Built Brihadisvara Temple.
  • Rajendra I: Expedition to Ganges and SE Asia.

Administration Mindmap

  • Central Government: King as supreme authority, aided by council.
  • Local Governance: Sabha (Brahmin assemblies) and Ur (General village assemblies).
  • Revenue: Kadamai (land tax) and Antarayam (other duties).
Assembly TypeMembershipFunction
UrGeneral villagersOrdinary village management
SabhaBrahmin landholdersAgrahara management/judicial

practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following Chola rulers initiated the naval expedition against the Srivijaya Empire?
practiceQuestions.sol: Rajendra I launched a successful naval expedition against the Srivijaya Empire to secure the sea routes to China.

practiceQuestions.q: The Uttaramerur inscription provides detailed information about the administration of which dynasty?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Uttaramerur inscription of Parantaka I provides deep insights into the Chola local self-government, particularly the working of the Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q: The term 'Kudavolai' during the Chola period referred to:
opts: A system of electing committee members
practiceQuestions.sol: The Kudavolai system was a lottery system used to elect members to various village committees (variyams) in the Chola local administration.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Chola king assumed the title 'Gangaikondachola'?
practiceQuestions.sol: Rajendra I assumed the title 'Gangaikondachola' after his victorious military campaign up to the banks of the river Ganges.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following was a prominent merchant guild during the Chola empire?
practiceQuestions.sol: Manigramam, along with Ayyavole and Anjuvannam, were powerful merchant guilds in South India during the Chola period.

practiceQuestions.q: The Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur was built by:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Brihadeeswarar Temple (Rajarajesvaram) was constructed by Rajaraja I and is a masterpiece of Dravidian architecture.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Chola ruler is known as 'Sungamtavirtta Cholan' for abolishing tolls?
practiceQuestions.sol: Kulottunga I abolished tolls to encourage trade and commerce, earning him the title 'Sungamtavirtta Cholan'.

practiceQuestions.q: In the Chola administrative system, a province was known as:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Chola empire was divided into Mandalams (provinces), Valanadus (divisions), Nadus (districts), and Kurrams (groups of villages).

practiceQuestions.q: The Chola bronze sculptures are predominantly made using which technique?
practiceQuestions.sol: Chola bronze sculptures, like the famous Nataraja, were made using the sophisticated lost-wax process.

practiceQuestions.q: Who was defeated at the Battle of Takkolam?
practiceQuestions.sol: Parantaka I suffered a major defeat at the hands of the Rashtrakuta king Krishna III at the Battle of Takkolam in 949 CE.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following pairs regarding Chola administration:
1. Ur: Assembly of Brahmins
2. Sabha: General assembly of the village
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
practiceQuestions.sol: Neither is correct. Ur was the general assembly of tax-paying villagers, while Sabha/Mahasabha was the assembly of Brahmins in Brahmadeya villages.

practiceQuestions.q: The compilation of Saiva hymns into 'Tirumurai' was undertaken by:
practiceQuestions.sol: Nambi Andar Nambi compiled the hymns of the Saiva Nayanmars into the Tirumurai during the reign of Rajaraja I.

practiceQuestions.q: The society under the Cholas saw the division of lower castes into:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Chola period witnessed the division of lower castes into Valangai (Right-hand) and Idangai (Left-hand) factions, a prominent social feature.

practiceQuestions.q: Which temple is a notable example of later Chola architecture, built by Rajaraja II?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram is a magnificent later Chola structure built by Rajaraja II.

practiceQuestions.q: Under the Cholas, the term 'Brahmadeya' referred to:
opts: A type of tax on agriculture
practiceQuestions.sol: Brahmadeya referred to tax-free lands gifted to Brahmins or a group of Brahmins.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Chola administration:
1. The empire was divided into Mandalams, which were further divided into Valanadus and Nadus.
2. The Kudavolai system was used to elect the members of the Ur.
3. The Uttaramerur inscription provides details on the qualifications required for members of the Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statement 2 is incorrect because the Kudavolai system was used to elect members for the committees (variyams) of the Sabha (Brahmin assembly), not the Ur (general assembly).

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to the history of India, consider the following pairs of guilds and their nature:
1. Manigramam: Agricultural cooperative
2. Ayyavole: Guild of itinerant merchants
3. Anjuvannam: Guild of foreign merchants
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Manigramam was a powerful guild of itinerant merchants, not an agricultural cooperative. Ayyavole (the Five Hundred) was a major inter-regional merchant guild, and Anjuvannam was associated with foreign traders.

mockTestQuestions.q: Rajendra I undertook a naval expedition against the Srivijaya Empire primarily because:
opts: He wanted to propagate Saivism in Southeast Asia.
Srivijaya kings had attacked the Chola coastal cities.
He wanted to remove obstacles placed by Srivijaya on Chola trade with China.
He was invited by a rival faction within the Srivijaya royal family.
mockTestQuestions.sol: The primary motivation was commercial. The Srivijaya empire controlled the Malacca Straits and was restricting Indian merchant guilds, threatening the lucrative Chola trade with Song dynasty China.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Chola art and architecture:
1. The Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur represents the zenith of the Nagara style of architecture.
2. Chola bronze sculptures were made using the 'lost-wax' technique.
3. The Vimana is the most prominent feature of Chola temples.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Brihadeeswarar Temple represents the Dravidian style of architecture, not Nagara.

mockTestQuestions.q: Which of the following statements about the Battle of Takkolam is correct?
opts: It was fought between Rajaraja I and the Cheras.
It resulted in a decisive victory for the Cholas over the Chalukyas.
It was a severe defeat for the Chola king Parantaka I at the hands of Rashtrakuta king Krishna III.
It marked the final collapse of the Pallava dynasty.
mockTestQuestions.sol: The Battle of Takkolam (949 CE) was a major setback for the early Imperial Cholas, where Rashtrakuta king Krishna III defeated Parantaka I.

mockTestQuestions.q: Regarding Chola society, the terms 'Valangai' and 'Idangai' refer to:
opts: Two major administrative divisions in the Chola empire.
Two rival factions among the lower castes.
Types of taxes levied on agricultural produce.
mockTestQuestions.sol: Valangai (Right-hand) and Idangai (Left-hand) were two broad and often antagonistic groupings of lower castes (especially agricultural and artisan classes) in Chola society.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Arrange the following Chola rulers in chronological order:
1. Rajendra I
2. Vijayalaya
3. Rajaraja I
4. Parantaka I
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
mockTestQuestions.sol: Vijayalaya (c. 850 CE) -> Parantaka I (c. 907 CE) -> Rajaraja I (c. 985 CE) -> Rajendra I (c. 1014 CE).

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding religion during the Chola period:
1. The Chola emperors were exclusively patrons of Vaishnavism.
2. Nambi Andar Nambi compiled the Saiva hymns into the Tirumurai.
3. Ramanuja, a Vaishnava philosopher, lived during the Chola period.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect; Chola emperors were ardent Saivites, though generally tolerant. Statements 2 and 3 are correct.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Match List-I (Temple) with List-II (Builder) and select the correct answer:
List-I:
A. Brihadeeswarar Temple, Thanjavur
B. Gangaikonda Cholapuram
C. Airavatesvara Temple, Darasuram

List-II:
1. Rajendra I
2. Rajaraja I
3. Rajaraja II
mockTestQuestions.sol: Brihadeeswarar was built by Rajaraja I; Gangaikonda Cholapuram by Rajendra I; Airavatesvara by Rajaraja II.

mockTestQuestions.q: Which of the following best describes the term 'Devadana' in the context of the Chola empire?
opts: A tax collected for the maintenance of temples.
A unit of currency used in maritime trade.
The personal bodyguard of the Chola king.
mockTestQuestions.sol: Devadana (or Tiruvidaiyattam) referred to tax-free lands gifted to temples for their maintenance and rituals.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the role of temples during the Chola period:
1. Temples functioned as banks, advancing loans to village assemblies.
2. Temples were major landholders and employers.
3. Education was imparted in the temple courtyards.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All statements are correct. Temples in the Chola period were massive socio-economic institutions. They acted as banks, major employers (priests, artisans, dancers), landowners, and centers of learning.

mockTestQuestions.q: Which of the following literary works was authored by Jayangondar to celebrate the military campaign of Kulottunga I?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Jayangondar wrote Kalingattuparani, a war poem detailing Kulottunga I's expedition against the kingdom of Kalinga.
